cls: Topical antiseptic / wound-debriding agent (iodophor with starch microbeads)
quick: Apply to a thickness of about 3 mm over the cleansed wound; change when saturated (color fades), up to 3x/week
Avoid - iodine absorption may affect fetal thyroid (especially large/prolonged use)
Avoid - iodine excreted in milk; risk to infant thyroid
Caution with extensive/prolonged use - iodine accumulation
Thyroid function with large-area/prolonged use; wound response; max 50 g per application, 150 g/week
summary: Cadexomer iodine is a topical wound product consisting of spherical hydrophilic starch (cadexomer) microbeads that carry iodine (0.9%). Applied to exuding chronic wounds (e.g., venous leg ulcers, pressure ulcers, infected wounds), the beads absorb exudate, bacteria, and debris while slowly releasing iodine to provide sustained, low-irritant antimicrobial action and to aid desloughing/debridement. The dressing changes from brown to grey/yellow as iodine is depleted, signaling the need for a change. Avoid in iodine sensitivity, thyroid disorders, and pregnancy/lactation, and limit total amount to reduce systemic iodine absorption.
indications: Cleansing and management of exuding chronic wounds such as venous leg ulcers, pressure ulcers (decubitus), and diabetic foot ulcers
Treatment of infected or sloughy wounds to reduce bacterial burden and absorb exudate

dosage.d: Apply to about 3 mm thickness over the cleansed wound bed
Do not exceed 50 g per single application
dosage.n: Do not exceed 150 g per week; limit total duration of continuous use

admin: Cleanse the wound (e.g., with saline) and remove loose debris before application
Apply cadexomer iodine to a depth of approximately 3 mm and cover with a secondary dressing
Change the dressing when it becomes saturated or when the brown color has faded to grey/yellow (iodine depleted)
Do not use on dry wounds (it requires exudate to function and may stick)
Remove by irrigation/rinsing; avoid forceful removal that damages new tissue
Limit treated surface area and total amount to minimize systemic iodine absorption
moa: Cadexomer iodine consists of hydrophilic spherical starch (cadexomer) microbeads in which iodine (0.9%) is incorporated. On contact with wound exudate the beads swell and absorb fluid, bacteria, slough, and debris (mechanical cleansing/desloughing), and this absorption gradually releases the bound iodine. The slowly liberated free iodine exerts broad-spectrum antimicrobial activity (bactericidal against gram-positive and gram-negative organisms, including MRSA, plus fungi) by oxidizing microbial proteins and nucleic acids, while the sustained low-concentration release limits cytotoxicity to healing tissue compared with aqueous iodine.

absolute: Thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism, nontoxic nodular goitre, Hashimoto thyroiditis)
relative: Large or deep wounds, or extensive body-surface application (greater iodine absorption)
Dry, low-exudate wounds (product needs moisture to work)
monitor: Thyroid function with prolonged or large-area use
Wound healing response and signs of irritation
Cumulative amount applied (per-application and weekly limits)

preg: Avoid during pregnancy. Absorbed iodine crosses the placenta and can affect the fetal thyroid (transient hypothyroidism/goitre), particularly with large wounds or prolonged use. Use only if no suitable alternative and benefit outweighs risk.
lact: Avoid during breastfeeding. Iodine is excreted in breast milk and may affect the infant's thyroid function. If treatment is essential, consider interrupting breastfeeding.
renal: Use with caution in renal impairment, especially for extensive or prolonged application, because reduced renal clearance can lead to iodine accumulation. Observe maximum amount and duration limits.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is required.

major: Lithium (additive risk of hypothyroidism with iodine - avoid)
moderate: Radioactive iodine / thyroid radioiodine uptake studies (iodine load interferes)
Other topical wound agents containing taurolidine, hydrogen peroxide, or silver (may inactivate or react)
interactions.diagnostics: Iodine absorption can interfere with thyroid function tests and radioiodine thyroid uptake studies

common: Transient local pain, stinging, or burning at the wound on application
serious: Altered thyroid function (hyper- or hypothyroidism) with prolonged/large-area use
Systemic iodine toxicity (iodism) with excessive absorption
rare: Metabolic disturbance (metabolic acidosis, electrolyte changes) with very extensive use
emergency: Thyroid storm or severe metabolic derangement from large systemic iodine absorption (very rare)

monitoring: Wound healing, exudate level, and signs of local irritation or infection
Thyroid function tests if used on large areas or for prolonged periods
Cumulative amount applied against per-application (50 g) and weekly (150 g) limits
counsel: This dressing cleans the wound and fights infection; it is for use on moist, exuding wounds
It is normal for the brown color to fade as it works - change the dressing when the color has faded or it is saturated
Mild stinging on application can occur and usually settles
Tell your clinician if you have thyroid disease, are pregnant or breastfeeding, or take lithium
Do not exceed the amount or duration your clinician advises
pk: Antimicrobial and exudate-absorbing action begins on contact with wound fluid
Iodine is released gradually as beads absorb exudate (sustained, not a sharp peak)
Not applicable for the topical product; absorbed iodine follows systemic iodine handling
One application remains active until the iodine is depleted (color fades) - often up to ~72 hours
Store at room temperature, protect from heat and light; keep dry until use
pearls: Not an FDA-approved drug entry in openFDA drug labels (cleared as a wound device/product, e.g., Iodosorb/Iodoflex) - record based on EU/SmPC and wound-care guidance
Color change from brown to grey/yellow is the practical signal that iodine is spent and the dressing needs changing
Dual action: starch microbeads absorb exudate, bacteria, and slough while slowly releasing antimicrobial iodine with relatively low tissue toxicity
Observe maximum limits (about 50 g per application, 150 g per week) and avoid in thyroid disease, pregnancy/lactation, and lithium use to limit systemic iodine effects
missed: Not applicable in the usual sense - reapply at the next scheduled dressing change. Change the dressing when it is saturated or the color has faded rather than on a strict clock schedule.
overdose: Excessive or prolonged use over large surfaces can cause systemic iodine absorption leading to thyroid dysfunction, iodism (metallic taste, sore mouth/throat, GI upset), and rarely metabolic acidosis or electrolyte disturbance. Management: discontinue use, irrigate/remove the product, check and support thyroid function and electrolytes, and provide supportive care.
refs: Cochrane / wound-care evidence - Cadexomer iodine for chronic wounds
